prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Customer Onboarding Field Validation Rules (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Field" · longest unbreakable word 126px · one-line width 126px
  col 2: header "Pattern" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 1074px
  col 3: header "Example valid" · longest unbreakable word 167px · one-line width 264px
  col 4: header "Error message" · longest unbreakable word 157px · one-line width 700px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference table for developers, QA and support to validate customer-onboarding fields: each row maps a field to its regex rule, a valid example, and the error copy shown on failure.","reading":"Readers look up rows by Field, then scan Pattern for implementation/testing and glance across to Example valid and Error message for concrete values and user-facing wording. Comparison is mainly within each row, not down numeric columns.","groups":["Field is the row key and identifier","Pattern and Example valid belong together as rule plus concrete instance","Example valid and Error message belong together as reader-facing validation feedback","Pattern is the technical column; Example valid and Error message are the human-facing columns"],"keep_intact":["snake_case field identifiers","regex atoms, character classes, quantifiers and anchors without mid-token breaks","example values such as emails, dates, currency amounts, slugs and VAT IDs","header words and error-message words"],"may_wrap":["long Pattern values at regex punctuation, alternation or quantifier boundaries","Error message prose at spaces","Example valid only at safe separators if necessary","multi-word headers at their space"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [147, 182, 188, 202] · table 720×849px · row heights [36, 222, 106, 83, 83, 129, 106, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [147, 190, 188, 194] · table 720×872px · row heights [36, 199, 129, 83, 83, 129, 129, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
